worksheet.title: Follow the Steps
worksheet.subtitle: Run the algorithm to make a pattern
worksheet.learning_goal: I can follow the steps of an algorithm to make a pattern.

parts.title: Run the algorithm
parts.text: Follow the steps in order, one at a time, to fill the boxes. Each step tells you which shape to draw in the next box. Running the steps makes a pattern.

parts.title: Follow the steps
parts.prompt: Do each step in order and draw ● or ■ in the boxes above. Read box 1 first, then box 2, and so on.

parts.title: Read your result
parts.prompt: What shape is in box 6? Draw it or write its name.

parts.title: You try — keep the pattern
parts.prompt: What is the pattern called (● ■ ● ■ …)? If there were a box 7, what shape would go there? Tell how you know.

parts.title: Big idea
parts.text: Running an algorithm means doing each step in order. The same steps always make the same result — here, a circle-square pattern.

parts.title: Goal
parts.text: Students execute a 6-step algorithm in order to fill a row of boxes, producing an AB (circle-square) pattern, then read the result and extend the pattern. Carrying out a sequence of steps to create a mathematical representation (a pattern) is C3.1; predicting the next term is reasoning about the outcome (C3.2).

parts.title: Ontario curriculum (Grade 1 — C3 Coding)
text: C3.1 — solve problems and create computational representations of mathematical situations by writing and executing code, including code that involves sequential events.
C3.2 — read and alter existing code, including code that involves sequential events, and describe how changes to the code affect the outcomes.

parts.title: Materials
parts.text: The printed worksheet and a pencil (red and blue crayons optional, to colour ● and ■). Optional: counters to lay out the pattern before drawing.

parts.title: Run it (about 20 min)
text: 1. I DO: read step 1 and draw ● in box 1. 'I do exactly what the step says, then go to the next step.'
2. WE DO: Exercise 1 — follow steps 2-6 together, drawing ■, ●, ■, ●, ■. Exercise 2 — box 6 is a square ■.
3. YOU DO: Exercise 3 — name the pattern (circle-square / AB) and predict box 7 (●).
4. Connect: 'A computer runs its steps in order, exactly — and the same steps always make the same pattern.'

parts.title: Answer key (modelled by the run-gate)
text: Ex 1 — boxes 1-6: ● ■ ● ■ ● ■ (circle, square, circle, square, circle, square).
Ex 3 — the pattern is circle-square, an AB pattern; box 7 would be a circle (●) because the pattern repeats ● then ■, and box 6 ended on ■.
Why it works: each step is carried out in order and only changes its own box, so the row always comes out the same.

parts.title: Watch for & differentiate
text: Common slip: skipping a box or doing steps out of order — have students touch each step and its box as they go.
Simplify: pre-draw boxes 1-2 together, then let students finish 3-6.
Extend: ask students to write a step 7 and step 8 that keep the pattern going (● then ■).
Success indicator: the child fills the boxes ● ■ ● ■ ● ■ and names the AB pattern, predicting box 7 as ●.
